title: City from Coordinates Finder: Name That Point
description: Get the city or nearest town for a bare coordinate pair with the City from Coordinates Finder — from the map's address record. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a GPS log entry at 40.7580, −73.9855 resolves to New York — the city field of the point's address record, no map-reading required.
quick_answer: The City from Coordinates Finder takes a bare latitude/longitude pair and returns the city (or nearest town) for that point from OpenStreetMap's address record. Paste the pair and read the settlement the record assigns — turning GPS logs and photo metadata back into named places.

Trackers and dashcams record numbers. This finder narrates them: which city each cluster of points belongs to.
A note that says only coordinates gets its municipal context — the settlement layer administrators file by.
A coordinates column audited against a claimed city column — mismatches surface the swapped and stale rows.
A point in open farmland has no containing city; the finder reports the nearest town the record supports, labelled as such. 'Near' is honest; pretending 'in' would not be.

popular_table.note: Settlement data is OpenStreetMap's community record: deep in populated regions, thinner where mapping is sparse. Administrative truth for legal purposes lives with authorities; this is the map's answer, fast and honest.

faq: What if the point is in the countryside?
The finder reports the nearest town the record supports, as 'nearest' — rural points get orientation, not a pretend municipality.
Which formats can I paste?
Decimal-degree pairs directly. DMS and other formats convert in seconds with the site's Coordinate Converter, then paste here.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — paste GPS and web-map coordinates as they come.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — the city answer is identical for a point and its six-decimal twin. Precision beyond the record's grain changes nothing here.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
The city name is text; the point stays coordinates. Both travel into GIS as attributes of the same feature.
Postal city versus governing city?
This finder reads administrative records — the governing settlement. Mail's 'city' follows postal geography and can differ, as the ZIP tools on this site explain.
It named a place I have never heard of.
Small municipalities hide inside famous metros' shadows. The record's answer is the point's actual settlement — often the day's geography lesson.
Ocean or lake points?
No city exists to name; the empty result is the correct one, and the Ocean or Land Checker formalises the question.
Batch of coordinates?
One at a time here; the Batch Geocoder resolves lists when the pile grows.
Towns versus cities — who decides?
The record's settlement classification. The finder reports the data's term rather than promoting villages for morale.
International points?
Worldwide where the address data reaches — settlement naming follows the record's local forms.
